record.original_question: Let A⊆N. For B⊆A, define lower and upper uniform, or Banach, densities by taking the limiting lower and upper proportions of B in long intervals, namely through the limits as s→∞ of the liminf and limsup over k of B(k+1,k+s)/s. Characterize the uniform-density set R_u(A)={(upper_u(B), lower_u(B)): B⊆A} for a fixed set A.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a set $X \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and integers $1 \le m \le n$, write $X(m,n) = |X \cap [m,n]|$. For real $s \ge 1$ define
$$\underline{\alpha}_s(X) = \liminf_{k\to\infty} X(k+1, k+s), \qquad \overline{\alpha}_s(X) = \limsup_{k\to\infty} X(k+1, k+s).$$
The lower uniform (Banach) density and upper uniform (Banach) density of $X$ are
$$\underline{u}(X) = \lim_{s\to\infty} \frac{\underline{\alpha}_s(X)}{s}, \qquad \overline{u}(X) = \lim_{s\to\infty} \frac{\overline{\alpha}_s(X)}{s}$$
(these limits exist by subadditivity/superadditivity).

Fix a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. Describe the set
$$R_u(A) = \{(\overline{u}(B), \underline{u}(B)) : B \subseteq A\} \subseteq [0,1]^2.$$
That is, give a characterization of which pairs $(x,y) \in [0,1]^2$ arise as $(\overline{u}(B), \underline{u}(B))$ for some subset $B$ of $A$.
artifact.status_search_result: A search returned foundational references on uniform/Banach density (e.g., the Grekos–Toma–Tomanová note in Annales Mathématiques Blaise Pascal and surveys on upper/lower densities), but no source giving a complete characterization of the uniform-density set $R_u(A)$ for an arbitrary fixed $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. The problem appears to remain open.
